beats.beat: The company processes and sells a wide range of specialty chemicals, primarily Functional Additives (FA) and Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), and also Soft Minerals and Hard Minerals.

It does not sell directly to end users. Instead, it has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through the promoter's established network.
Customer concentration is high: its top ten customers accounted for about 59% of revenue from operations in each of the three financial years through March 2017.
The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka, with aggregate exports of ₹1068.18 lakh over the past five years.

The DRHP lists six competitive strengths: diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution, support from the holding company, product innovation and R&D, and a strong management team.

beats.beat: Profit after tax turned positive in fiscal 2015 after two years of losses: ₹(27.40) lakh in FY2013, ₹(12.17) lakh in FY2014, then ₹149.58 lakh in FY2015, ₹90.18 lakh in FY2016, ₹174.82 lakh in FY2017, and ₹132.75 lakh in the six months ended September 2017.

Operating cash flow has been volatile: ₹200.97 lakh in FY2013, ₹127.73 lakh in FY2014, ₹422.36 lakh in FY2015, ₹802.59 lakh in FY2016, a negative ₹(349.75) lakh in FY2017, and ₹124.86 lakh in H1 FY2018.
Total assets grew from ₹2,679.38 lakh as at March 2013 to ₹3,424.96 lakh as at March 2017, then dipped to ₹3,018.66 lakh as at September 2017.
Basic earnings per share improved from negative to positive: (₹0.45) in FY2013, (₹0.20) in FY2014, ₹2.47 in FY2015, ₹1.46 in FY2016, ₹2.43 in FY2017, and ₹1.48 in H1 FY2018.

beats.beat: The company has four promoters: three individuals – Chandresh S. Parikh, Atil C. Parikh, and Rajesh C. Parikh – and the corporate entity 20 Microns Limited.
Promoters together hold 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up equity capital (89,48,270 equity shares of ₹10 each). The promoter group (excluding promoters) holds the remaining 0.24% (21,510 shares).
The company has entered into related-party transactions in each of the last five financial years and the six months ended September 2017, as per Accounting Standard 18.
There have been instances of non-filing or delayed filing of statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies, subsequently rectified with additional fees.

The company has not yet obtained certain statutory licenses for its manufacturing facility at Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia, and does not own the premises for its other two manufacturing facilities and two administrative offices.

beats.beat: Specialty chemicals (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) account for about 17% of India's chemicals industry, with an estimated market size of around ₹1,000 billion in fiscal 2017.
The segment grew at 10–12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017, and CRISIL Research expects it to grow at 12–14% CAGR going forward.
The industry is highly fragmented: small and medium enterprises hold 70–75% of the market, and only a few Indian players can compete with global giants on product development.

Within specialty chemicals, sub-segments have distinct growth projections: construction chemicals and water chemicals at 15% CAGR, polymer additives at 10%, surfactants at 13%, and textiles and flavours & fragrances at 12%.
Key regulatory drivers include 100% FDI approval, a Draft National Chemical Policy, the GST implementation from July 2017, and REACH compliance for exports to Europe.

beats.beat: No long-term agreements: The company has no long-term or definitive contracts with customers or raw-material suppliers; all sales are on purchase orders, and supplies can be disrupted.
Missing regulatory approvals: The company has not obtained all required statutory licenses for its Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia manufacturing facility, exposing it to potential penalties.
Negative cash flows: The company reported negative operating cash flow in FY2017 (₹(349.75) lakh) and had net losses in FY2013 and FY2014, which could constrain growth and working capital.
Intense competition: The specialty chemicals market is fragmented with SMEs holding 70–75% share, and global giants compete in product development, leading to pricing pressure.
Legal proceedings: The company, its promoters, group companies, and directors are parties to certain legal proceedings; an adverse outcome could materially affect the business.
